versions.changelog:
- Expanded and clarified trigger conditions for when to use the skill, emphasizing user questioning and tool anomalies.
- Enhanced trigger descriptions to include more concrete detection signals and keywords (e.g., "你确定吗", "review", "verify").
- Made instructions and verification steps more explicit, emphasizing a critical review that covers all six audit questions.
- Added sections on Verification and self-optimization, specifying concrete actions if verification fails or succeeds.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.

- Clarified the purpose and triggers for using assess-me: only for cognitive audits, not regular use.
- Added a detailed “Triggers” section (with tiered table), specifying when and why to activate the skill, including new examples and reasoning states.
- Refined the description to highlight uncertainty, contradiction, ambiguity, and unverified assumptions as activation criteria.
- Removed skill-card.md file.

- Initial release of the assess-me skill for auditing your current thinking process during stuck or confusing problem-solving.
- Guides users to systematically answer 6 key questions (Goal, Progress, Gaps, Assumptions, Blocker, Recovery) and record responses to a temporary file.
- Adds a review step: read back your own answers to promote critical detachment and identify mistakes or weak points.
- Enforces best practices: always list assumptions, avoid vague blockers, and make recovery plans concrete.
- Output includes a standardized summary block for quick reference.
